name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q01 - Chances of contracting bird flu from cooked poultry

questiontext.text: The chances of contacting bird flu from a properly cooked (above 100°C) chicken and egg are:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Bird flu (avian influenza) is caused by the avian influenza virus (such as H5N1 strain), which is highly sensitive to heat.

Step 2: Thermal Inactivation
Viruses and their proteins are denatured and inactivated at high temperatures. Cooking poultry meat and eggs properly at temperatures exceeding 100°C effectively destroys the virus in all parts of the food.

Step 3: Conclusion
Because standard cooking conditions thoroughly kill the virus, the likelihood of contracting bird flu from properly cooked chicken and eggs is negligible.

Final Answer:
negligible

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q02 - Definition of a breed in animal husbandry

questiontext.text: A group of animals which are related by descent and share many similarities are referred to as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Definition in Animal Husbandry
In animal husbandry, a breed is defined as a specific group of domestic animals related by descent and possessing similar general appearance, features, size, and configuration.

Step 2: Comparison with Other Taxonomic Terms
Species is the fundamental taxonomic unit for sexually reproducing organisms in nature. Variety is a taxonomic rank typically applied to plants. Race refers to genetically distinct geographical populations. For domesticated livestock, individuals related by lineage and sharing common characteristics belong to a breed.

Step 3: Conclusion
A group of animals related by descent and sharing many similar morphological and physiological characters is called a breed.

Final Answer:
breed

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q03 - Genetic objective and effect of inbreeding

questiontext.text: Inbreeding is carried out in animal husbandry because it:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle of Inbreeding
Inbreeding involves the mating of closely related individuals within the same breed for 4 to 6 generations.

Step 2: Genetic Consequences
Mating related individuals increases the probability that offspring inherit identical alleles from a common ancestor, thereby increasing homozygosity. This enables the expression and elimination of harmful recessive alleles through selection and helps in establishing purelines.

Step 3: Conclusion
The primary genetic outcome of inbreeding in animal breeding programs is to increase homozygosity.

Final Answer:
increases homozygosity

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q04 - Crop identity of Sonalika and Kalyan Sona

questiontext.text: Sonalika and Kalyan Sona are varieties of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Historical Agricultural Context
During the Green Revolution in India in 1963, semi-dwarf, high-yielding selections were introduced to enhance food grain production.

Step 2: Origin and Classification
Semi-dwarf wheat strains originally developed by Norman E. Borlaug at CIMMYT in Mexico were adapted for Indian cultivation. Sonalika and Kalyan Sona were two widely cultivated, high-yielding, and disease-resistant varieties of wheat introduced across the wheat-growing belt of India.

Step 3: Conclusion
Sonalika and Kalyan Sona are prominent varieties of wheat.

Final Answer:
wheat

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q05 - Identifying the non fungal plant disease

questiontext.text: Which one of the following is not a fungal disease?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Classification of Plant Pathogens
Plant diseases are caused by various microbial pathogens including fungi, bacteria, and viruses.

Step 2: Causative Agents of Listed Diseases
Rust of wheat is caused by the fungus Puccinia graminis.
Smut of bajra is caused by the fungus Tolyposporium penicillariae.
Red rot of sugarcane is caused by the fungus Colletotrichum falcatum.
Black rot of crucifers is caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas campestris.

Step 3: Conclusion
Among the listed diseases, black rot of crucifers is caused by a bacterial pathogen rather than a fungus.

Final Answer:
Black rot of crucifers

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q06 - Mechanism of virus free plant meristems

questiontext.text: In virus-infected plants the meristematic tissues in both apical and axillary buds are free of virus because:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principle of Meristem Culture
Even in systemically infected plants, the apical and axillary shoot meristems are generally virus-free.

Step 2: Biological Mechanism
Meristematic cells undergo rapid, continuous mitotic divisions. The rate of cell division in the meristem exceeds the rate of viral multiplication and systemic translocation. In addition, the lack of differentiated vascular tissue in the apical dome restricts the movement of viral particles into the meristem.

Step 3: Conclusion
The meristematic zone remains free of virus because meristem cell division occurs faster than viral replication and spread.

Final Answer:
the cell division of meristems are faster than the rate of viral multiplication

answer.text: the cell division of meristems are faster than the rate of viral multiplication

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q07 - Agronomic trait enabling multiple rice crops

questiontext.text: Several South Indian states raise 2-3 crops of rice annually. The agronomic feature that makes this possible is because of

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Agronomic Principle of Multiple Cropping
Cultivating two to three cycles of a cereal crop within a single year on the same land requires varieties with a reduced maturation period.

Step 2: Trait Evaluation
Early yielding rice varieties have a short lifecycle from sowing to harvest. This abbreviated duration allows farmers to fit multiple successive growing cycles into the annual agricultural calendar under favorable climatic conditions.

Step 3: Conclusion
The agronomic characteristic that permits harvesting two to three rice crops per year is the early yielding nature of the rice variety.

Final Answer:
early yielding rice variety

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q08 - Desirable agronomic traits for sugarcane cultivation

questiontext.text: Which one of the following combination would a sugarcane farmer look for in the sugarcane crop?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Agricultural Goals in Sugarcane Farming
Sugarcane is grown for commercial sucrose extraction from the stem tissues.

Step 2: Evaluation of Yield Components
Thick stems provide greater volume of juice per cane.
Long internodes increase the total stalk length and overall biomass yield.
High sugar content ensures maximum sucrose recovery per ton of harvested cane.
Disease resistance prevents fungal infections such as red rot, protecting crop yield.
Profuse flowering is undesirable because flowering terminates vegetative stem growth and reduces sucrose content.

Step 3: Conclusion
The ideal combination of traits sought by a sugarcane grower includes thick stem, long internodes, high sugar content, and disease resistance.

Final Answer:
Thick stem, long internodes, high sugar content and disease resistant

answer.text: Thick stem, long internodes, high sugar content and disease resistant
Thick stem, high sugar content and profuse flowering
Thick stem, short internodes, high sugar content, disease resistant
Thick stem, low sugar, conten, disease resistant

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q09 - Target specificity of fungicides and antibiotics

questiontext.text: Fungicides and antibiotics are chemicals that:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Chemical Definitions
Antimicrobial chemicals are named based on the class of pathogen they target.

Step 2: Specificity of Action
Fungicides are biocidal chemical compounds designed to destroy or inhibit fungal organisms.
Antibiotics are antimicrobial substances that selectively inhibit or kill bacterial pathogens.

Step 3: Conclusion
Fungicides kill pathogenic fungi and antibiotics kill pathogenic bacteria, respectively.

Final Answer:
kill pathogenic fungi and bacteria, respectively

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q10 - Definition of mutation breeding in crop plants

questiontext.text: Use of certain chemicals and radiation to change the base sequences of genes of crop plants is termed:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Definition of Mutation in Crop Improvement
Mutations are heritable alterations in nucleotide base sequences of DNA that create new genetic variability.

Step 2: Methodology
Using physical agents (like gamma radiation) or chemical mutagens to deliberately induce mutations, followed by screening and selection for desirable agronomic traits, is called mutation breeding.

Step 3: Conclusion
Inducing changes in gene base sequences using chemicals or radiation to breed improved crops is known as mutation breeding.

Final Answer:
mutation breeding

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q11 - Process of nutrient enrichment in crop plants

questiontext.text: The scientific process by which crop plants are enriched with certain desirable nutrients is called:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Breeding crops to address micronutrient deficiencies and hidden hunger is a major branch of modern agricultural biotechnology.

Step 2: Terminology
Bio-fortification refers to breeding food crops with higher levels of essential vitamins, minerals, proteins, and healthier fats.
Bio-remediation is the use of organisms to remove environmental pollutants, while crop protection involves shielding crops from pests and pathogens.

Step 3: Conclusion
The enrichment of crop plants with desirable nutritional components is termed bio-fortification.

Final Answer:
bio-fortification

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q12 - Definition of cellular totipotency in plants

questiontext.text: The term 'totipotency' refers to the capacity of a:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Cellular Concept of Totipotency
Totipotency is an intrinsic property demonstrated by living nucleated plant cells in tissue culture.

Step 2: Biological Capability
Totipotency is the genetic capacity of a single isolated plant cell to divide, differentiate, and develop into a complete, functioning plant when supplied with appropriate nutrient media and growth regulators under sterile conditions.

Step 3: Conclusion
The term totipotency refers to the ability of an individual cell to regenerate an entire plant.

Final Answer:
cell to generate whole plant

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q13 - Correct statements regarding somatic hybridization technique

questiontext.text:
Given below are a few statements regarding somatic hybridization. Choose the correct statements.

  1. protoplasts of different cells of the same plant are fused
  2. protoplasts from cells of different species can be fused
  3. treatment of cells with cellulase and pectinase is mandatory
  4. the hybrid protoplast contains characters of only one parental protoplast.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principle of Somatic Hybridization
Somatic hybridization involves isolating naked protoplasts from cells of different varieties or species and fusing them to produce a hybrid plant carrying traits of both parents.

Step 2: Evaluation of Biological Conditions
Plant cell walls contain cellulose and pectin. Enzymatic removal of the rigid cell wall requires digestion with cellulase and pectinase enzymes, making this enzymatic treatment mandatory for protoplast isolation.
Protoplasts derived from cells of different species can be fused using fusogens such as polyethylene glycol, allowing sexual incompatibility barriers to be bypassed.
Fusing cells from the same plant does not yield a hybrid, and a somatic hybrid protoplast combines cytoplasmic and nuclear characteristics from both parental cells rather than only one.

Step 3: Conclusion
The valid statements are that protoplasts from cells of different species can be fused, and treatment of cells with cellulase and pectinase is mandatory.

Final Answer:
(ii) and (iii)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q14 - Definition of an explant in tissue culture

questiontext.text: An explant is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Plant Tissue Culture Terminology
Tissue culture requires initiating in vitro cultures from excised plant pieces under sterile conditions.

Step 2: Technical Meaning of Explant
An explant is any excised piece of plant tissue—such as shoot tip, node, leaf segment, root tip, or embryo—that is removed from a donor plant, surface-sterilized, and inoculated onto a nutrient culture medium.

Step 3: Conclusion
An explant is specifically that part of a plant excised and used to initiate in vitro tissue culture.

Final Answer:
part of the plant used in tissue culture

answer.text: part of the plant used in tissue culture
part of the plant that expresses a specific gene.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q15 - Primary constraint in conventional plant breeding

questiontext.text: The biggest constraint of plant breeding is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of Conventional Plant Breeding
Conventional breeding is limited to the preexisting genetic variability present in the gene pool of a crop species and its wild relatives.

Step 2: Analysis of Constraints
If a specific desirable trait (such as resistance to a particular pathogen or drought tolerance) is not present as a functional allele anywhere in the cultivated varieties or sexually compatible wild relatives, conventional hybridization cannot introduce it into the crop.

Step 3: Conclusion
The greatest constraint in plant breeding is the limited availability of desirable genes within the gene pool of the crop and its wild relatives.

Final Answer:
availability of desirable gene in the crop and its wild relatives

answer.text: availability of desirable gene in the crop and its wild relatives

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q16 - Nutritional classification of lysine and tryptophan

questiontext.text: Lysine and tryptophan are:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Nutritional Classification of Amino Acids
Amino acids that cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be acquired through diet are designated as essential amino acids.

Step 2: Classification of Lysine and Tryptophan
Both lysine and tryptophan are essential amino acids. In addition, conventional cereal grains are naturally deficient in lysine and tryptophan, prompting breeding initiatives to biofortify maize and other cereals with higher levels of these two essential amino acids.

Step 3: Conclusion
Lysine and tryptophan are classified as essential amino acids.

Final Answer:
essential amino acids

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q17 - Definition and technique of plant micropropagation

questiontext.text: Micro-propagation is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Meaning of Micro-propagation
Micro-propagation is the method of mass-producing plants under laboratory conditions using tissue culture.

Step 2: Methodological Description
By culturing small explants on artificial nutrient medium under aseptic conditions, thousands of genetically identical whole plants (somaclones) can be generated rapidly from a single parent plant.

Step 3: Conclusion
Micro-propagation is defined as the in vitro propagation of plants.

Final Answer:
propagation of plants in vitro

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q18 - Structural definition of a plant protoplast

questiontext.text: Protoplast is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Plant Cell Structure
A normal plant cell consists of an external protective cell wall enclosing the living contents.

Step 2: Definition of Protoplast
When the cellulosic and pectic cell wall is removed either mechanically or enzymatically, the living cell structure that remains bounded solely by the plasma membrane is designated as a protoplast.

Step 3: Conclusion
A protoplast is a plant cell stripped of its surrounding cell wall.

Final Answer:
a plant cell without a cell wall

answer.text: a plant cell without a cell wall

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q19 - Required enzymes for isolating plant protoplasts

questiontext.text: To isolate protoplast, one needs:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Composition of the Plant Cell Wall
The plant cell wall consists of cellulose microfibrils embedded in a matrix of pectin, with middle lamellae composed primarily of calcium pectate.

Step 2: Enzymatic Cleavage
To release intact protoplasts, pectinase is needed to break down the intercellular cementing pectin substances, and cellulase is needed to digest the cellulose fibers of the primary wall. Chitinase acts on fungal cell walls and is not utilized for plant cells.

Step 3: Conclusion
Isolating naked plant protoplasts requires the concerted action of both pectinase and cellulase enzymes.

Final Answer:
both pectinase and cellulase

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q20 - Identification of commercial marine fish species

questiontext.text: Which one of the following is a marine fish:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Aquatic Habitats of Commercial Fishes
Fishes raised or harvested in fisheries are divided into freshwater and marine groups based on natural habitat.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Fishes Listed
Rohu (Labeo rohita), Catla (Catla catla), and Common Carp (Cyprinus carpio) are widely cultured freshwater species.
Hilsa (Tenualosa ilisha), along with sardine, mackerel, and pomfret, is a major commercial marine fish.

Step 3: Conclusion
Among the given choices, Hilsa is a marine fish.

Final Answer:
Hilsa

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q21 - Apiculture product used in cosmetics and polishes

questiontext.text: Which one of the following products of apiculture is used in cosmetics and polishes:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Apicultural Products
Beekeeping produces several commercial commodities including honey, beeswax, propolis, and royal jelly.

Step 2: Industrial Uses of Beeswax
Beeswax is secreted by the wax glands of worker honeybees to build honeycomb cells. Due to its lipid composition and emollient properties, it is extensively used in the preparation of cosmetics (creams, ointments, lipsticks) and polishes.

Step 3: Conclusion
The product of apiculture used in the cosmetic and polish industries is beeswax.

Final Answer:
wax

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q22 - Global distribution of the livestock population

questiontext.text: More than 70 per cent of livestock population is found in:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: World Livestock Statistics
Livestock farming is distributed across the globe, but cattle, buffalo, and other livestock populations are heavily concentrated in specific regions.

Step 2: Demographic Share
According to agricultural data recorded in NCERT, India and China collectively house more than 70 percent of the total livestock population of the world, although their share of global farm output is approximately 25 percent.

Step 3: Conclusion
More than 70 per cent of the world's livestock is found in India and China.

Final Answer:
India and China.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q23 - Percentage of Indian population employed in agriculture

questiontext.text: The agriculture sector of India employs about:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Socio-economic Role of Agriculture in India
Agriculture represents the largest employment sector for the population of India.

Step 2: Demographic Data
NCERT figures record that agriculture accounts for roughly 33 percent of India's GDP and employs approximately 62 percent (around 60 percent) of the total population.

Step 3: Conclusion
The agricultural sector of India employs approximately 60 per cent of the population.

Final Answer:
60 per cent of the population.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q24 - Contribution of agriculture to Indian gross product

questiontext.text: 33 percent of India's Gross Domestic Product comes from

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Macroeconomic Role of Agriculture
Agriculture is a foundational pillar of the Indian economy.

Step 2: GDP Contribution
As stated in NCERT, agriculture contributes approximately 33 percent to India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) while supporting around 62 percent of the country's workforce.

Step 3: Conclusion
Thirty-three percent of India's Gross Domestic Product comes from agriculture.

Final Answer:
Agriculture

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q25 - Definition of germplasm collection in breeding

questiontext.text: A collection of all the alleles of all the genes of a crop plant is called:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Genetic Resource Conservation
Genetic diversity is essential for successful plant breeding and crop improvement programs.

Step 2: Definition of Germplasm Collection
The complete collection of seeds, plants, or tissues representing all the diverse alleles of all the genes in a given crop species and its wild relatives is defined as a germplasm collection. An herbarium is a repository of dried, preserved plant specimens, not live genetic material.

Step 3: Conclusion
The comprehensive collection of all alleles of all genes in a crop plant is designated as a germplasm collection.

Final Answer:
germplasm collection
